I'm the fast assistant for this session; you're on /framework/ai/2026-09-30/dictation-stream/.
A chat bubble is the rounded box that holds a single message in a conversation. Each bubble sits to one side, which shows who said it, so a reader can follow the exchange at a glance.
Still the automated streaming test: answer from memory with no tools, in about 150 words of plain prose, how a chat app shows a reply while it is being written. Do not start any work.

A chat app shows a reply while it is being written by streaming it. The server doesn't wait for the whole answer. It sends the text in small pieces, called tokens or chunks, as soon as the model produces each one. The connection stays open, usually through server-sent events or a WebSocket, and every new piece arrives as its own small message.

When the first piece arrives, the app draws an empty bubble on screen and appends each new piece to that bubble's text. It usually re-renders the text as it goes, so formatting like bold words or lists shows up partway through. A blinking cursor or a typing dot often marks the end of the text, which tells the reader the reply isn't finished. When the server sends a final "done" signal, the app removes the cursor and saves the reply. If the stream breaks partway, the app keeps what arrived and shows an error or a retry button.
